No. The audit reads and reports only. The Premium package includes up to three sample fixes, which arrive as a separate pull request that you can accept or ignore.
What do you need from me?
A zip or repository access, and the WooCommerce and PHP versions you aim to support. A short note on your biggest worry, such as a slow admin page, helps us aim the review.
Does the audit include a security review?

It covers the common weaknesses, such as missing escaping, nonces, capability checks and unsafe queries. It is a code review, not a full penetration test, and the report says what it did and did not cover.

desc:
A WooCommerce plugin code audit is a careful review of your plugin for security, speed, standards and compatibility. Ecom Swift LLC reads the code, runs the checks and sends a written report that ranks every finding by effort and impact.

## What is a WooCommerce plugin code audit?

It is an independent read-through of a plugin's source code, backed by automated checks. The reviewer looks for mistakes that could harm a store, such as missing escaping, missing nonces, weak permission checks and slow queries. The output is a report, not a code change.

Think of it as a pre-release inspection. You learn what is wrong, how serious it is and what to fix first, before store owners or a directory reviewer find the problems for you.

## Why do plugin problems stay hidden until it is too late?

Most plugin bugs do not show up during normal use. A missing nonce check works perfectly until someone tricks a logged-in admin into clicking a crafted link. A query that scans a whole table feels fine on a small test store and falls over on a store with years of orders.

Developers also get used to their own code. After many months, small shortcuts look normal. A fresh reader notices them straight away and can explain why they matter.

## How an audit protects your plugin and users

A plugin that handles orders and customer details is a target. A single unescaped field can lead to injected scripts in the admin. Fixing such an issue before release is far cheaper than responding to a report from users.

The same goes for speed. Hooks that run on every page load and queries that run inside loops slow down every store that installs the plugin. A ranked list lets your team spend limited time where it improves reliability the most.

## What a thorough audit includes

- An automated scan against the WordPress coding standards.
- Review of escaping on output and sanitizing on input.
- Checks for nonces and capability checks on every form and action.
- Review of database queries and hooks for speed.
- Compatibility checks with current WooCommerce, High-Performance Order Storage and recent PHP versions.
- A look at the plugin against the WordPress.org plugin guidelines.
- Block checkout compatibility, where the plugin touches checkout.
- Review of uninstall and data cleanup behavior.
- Findings ranked by effort and impact, in plain language.
- A fix roadmap with estimates, in higher packages.

## What we do

You send the plugin code. We install it on a clean test site, run the automated checks and then read the code by hand, starting with the places that handle input, output, payments and stored data.

Each finding in the report names the file and the problem, explains the risk in plain words and suggests a fix. We rank them so you can see quick wins separately from larger jobs. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in depth, the number of ranked findings, whether speed and compatibility checks are included and the length of the review call. Larger packages add a fix roadmap and a few sample fixes so your developer can see the pattern.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Share the version you plan to release, not an old copy.
- Tell us which areas worry you most.
- Give your developer time to read the report with us on a call.
- Fix high-impact findings first, then re-check.
- Keep the report as a checklist for future releases.

**Avoid:**
- Treating the audit as a pass or fail stamp.
- Fixing only the easy items and leaving serious ones.
- Sending code that has been minified or obfuscated.
- Auditing right before a deadline, with no time left to fix.
- Assuming that one audit covers every future version.

## Who this service is for

This service suits a plugin author preparing a first public release who wants a second pair of eyes. It suits an agency that inherited a client plugin and does not know its quality. It also suits a store owner who relies on a custom plugin and wants to know whether it is safe.

## What we need from you

Send the plugin as a zip or a repository link, plus a short note on what it does and where it is used. We do not change your plugin during the audit. We never ask for passwords, and a live store login is not needed. If you want us to fix findings afterwards, we can quote that as separate work.
